guide.forced_release_form.read_the_plan_: (read the plan in the Release view first)
guide.forced_release_form.the_release_vi: the Release view lists the packages no commit releases
guide.forced_release_form.no_commit_sinc: no commit since its last release releases it
guide.forced_release_form.smith_release_: smith release --bump <package>=<level> --force: the same code under a new version
guide.forced_release_form.which_package_: Which package should release without a releasing commit?
guide.install_package_form.install_into_: Install into which projects? (Space ticks, Enter confirms). Each project uses its own package manager, so tick projects of one language when the name is the same in every registry.
guide.install_package_form.which_package: Which packages? Type a name or name@version; separate several with spaces.
guide.install_package_form.installs_into: Installs into projects, or the workspace root where it is offered. A tool installed on the machine (npm -g) has no smith command yet.
guide.install_package_form.the_project_n: the project needs it when it runs (the default)
guide.install_package_form.only_for_buil: only for building and testing (smith install -D). Peer and optional have no flag yet.
guide.parity_forms.names_to_add_separate: Names to add, separated by commas (lowercase words, such as qa, stage)
guide.parity_forms.each_name_gets_a_env_: Each name gets a .env.<name> file, a build:<name> task and an output folder. The plan shows the files before they are written.
guide.parity_forms.names_to_remove_separ: Names to remove, separated by commas (smith environments list shows them)
guide.parity_forms.the_env_name_file_sta: The .env.<name> file stays, because it holds your values. The default environment cannot be removed.
guide.parity_forms.smith_pipeline_a_pipe: smith pipeline: a pipeline file beside the generated CI; it is yours from then on and smith upgrade never rewrites it
guide.parity_forms.make_the_icons_of_a_t: Make the icons of a Tauri app
guide.parity_forms.smith_tauri_icon_ever: smith tauri icon: every icon size from one square PNG; the plan lists the files it overwrites
guide.parity_forms.which_square_png_a_pa: Which square PNG? (a path from where you started smith)
guide.parity_forms.which_app_only_when_m: Which app? (only when more than one has a src-tauri; Enter leaves it out)
guide.parity_forms.smith_docker_descript: smith docker description: the description of each app's image on Docker Hub
guide.parity_forms.default_nothing_is_se: default: nothing is sent to Docker Hub
guide.parity_forms.calls_docker_hub_with: calls Docker Hub with your login
guide.parity_forms.why_would_a_task_run_: Why would a task run again?
guide.parity_forms.smith_why_miss_why_a_: smith why-miss: why a task did not come from the cache
guide.parity_forms.connect_smith_to_a_co: Connect smith to a coding assistant
guide.parity_forms.smith_mcp_install_wri: smith mcp install: writes the file that lets the assistant start smith's MCP server
guide.plugin_search_form.do_you_trust_th: Do you trust this plugin? A plugin runs with your privileges and smith does not sandbox it
guide.plugin_search_form.nothing_runs_no: nothing runs now; smith asks the first time the plugin is used
guide.plugin_search_form.install_trust_a: Install, trust and pin this version
guide.plugin_search_form.it_may_run_at_o: it may run at once; smith writes the SHA-256 of its program to smith.toml, and CI refuses a changed file (--trust --pin)
guide.plugin_search_form.which_plugin_ty: Which plugin? (type to narrow the list)
guide.web_environments_steps.a_web_app_i: A web app is built once per environment. Which environments?
guide.web_environments_steps.vite_writes: Vite writes its VITE_ values into the bundle when it builds, so each environment is its own build with its own .env file.
guide.web_environments_steps.you_type_th: you type the names (lowercase words, such as qa, stage), then say which one smith run build builds
guide.web_environments_steps.which_envir: which environment smith run build builds, where the builds go, and whether the .env files are kept in git
guide.web_environments_steps.smith_add_e: smith add --environments none: a single vite build, as before
guide.web_environments_steps.which_envir: Which environment is `smith run build`? CI and the release build this one
guide.web_environments_steps.default_dis: default: dist/apps/<app>/<name>, with every other build
guide.web_environments_steps.dist_name_i: dist/<name> in the app's own folder; smith doctor then accepts it
guide.web_environments_steps.the_env_fil: The .env files hold VITE_ values, which end up in the browser, so no secret. Keep them in git?
guide.web_environments_steps.yes_keep_th: Yes, keep the .env files in git
guide.web_environments_steps.each_machin: each machine and CI job makes its own files; git ignores them
guide.forced_release.title: Release without a releasing commit
guide.forced_release.not_offered: Not offered, because smith has no version to bump: {names} (never released). To choose the first version, commit: git commit --allow-empty -m "version({first})[1.0.0]"
guide.install_package.root: Workspace root: shared by every project, in the root package.json
guide.install_package.title: Install a package
guide.install_package.option: {name} is an option, not a package: the next question sets the kind
guide.parity_forms.add_title: Add environments to a web app
guide.parity_forms.remove_title: Remove environments from a web app
guide.parity_forms.hint: smith environments {verb}: the plan comes first; the .env files you wrote stay
guide.plugin_search.unreadable: smith plugin search did not print a list of plugins
guide.plugin_search.title: Find a plugin in the marketplace
guide.plugin_search.install_title: Install a plugin from the marketplace
guide.remove_package.title: Remove {name}
guide.remove_package.which: {name} is declared in more than one project. Remove it from which? (Space ticks, Enter confirms)
guide.web_environments.use_these_hint: smith run build builds prd, the builds go to dist/apps/<name>/<env>, and the .env files are written for you and kept in git (smith commits nothing)
guide.web_environments.change_details: Change the build default, the output or the .env files…
